incidents.vector: Attackers forged authentication-override cookies to bypass authentication on PAN-OS GlobalProtect portals/gateways (CVE-2026-0257) where the same certificate was reused for HTTPS and cookie encryption.
incidents.impact: Successful exploitation observed across multiple customer environments starting May 17, with a second wave on May 21; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and some attackers gained internal network access.

incidents.vector: Cloud storage server left publicly accessible without a password.
incidents.impact: More than 3.4 million scanned images — including driver's licenses, legal documents, and financial records tied to inmate calls — were exposed online for at least a week before the bucket was secured.

incidents.victim: Enterprises using npm (including Sberbank brand abuse)
incidents.vector: A single operator using three npm maintainer aliases (mr.4nd3r50n, ce-rwb, t-in-one) published 43 malicious packages across nine corporate scopes — including one impersonating Sberbank's SberPay widget — exploiting dependency confusion to win resolution against real internal packages.
incidents.impact: Each install triggered an obfuscated post-install reconnaissance payload that fingerprinted developer environments and exfiltrated context to a C2 server, with a flag in the design to escalate from recon to full exploitation later; packages were taken down after Microsoft's report to npm.

incidents.vector: Phishing compromised a single employee account, granting access to a portion of Carnival's IT environment in April.
incidents.impact: Personal data on roughly 6 million people — including names, addresses, dates of birth, driver's license and passport numbers — was copied; the attackers later released 8.7M records claimed to include Holland America Mariner Society loyalty data.

incidents.vector: Silent Ransom Group impersonates IT support via phone and phishing, and — uniquely among ransomware-class actors — physically dispatches associates to victim offices to attach storage devices to workstations when remote access attempts fail.
incidents.impact: FBI issued a renewed alert; the group has claimed more than 100 attacks with activity surging in recent months, primarily against the legal sector; Halcyon tracked 134 ransomware incidents against law firms in Q1 2026.

incidents.vector: Hacker exploited an unpatched vulnerability in the club's systems (original breach disclosed March 2026).
incidents.impact: Dutch police arrested a 35-year-old in Buren on suspicion of intrusion; the breach reportedly may have exposed personal information of over 300,000 registered Ajax supporters and affected more than 42,000 season tickets.

incidents.victim: Oregon state government office (and other US victims)
incidents.vector: Catalin Dragomir, 46, of Romania, gained unauthorized access to an Oregon state office computer in June 2021 and sold network access plus samples of personal data to other criminals.
incidents.impact: Sentenced to 56 months in US federal prison; total losses from his activity exceeded $250,000 across multiple US victims.

incidents.vector: TD Bank employee Cheungkin Lam accepted bribes to identify high-balance accounts, leak confidential customer information to outside co-conspirators, and bribe an employee of another bank to falsify records.
incidents.impact: Facilitated more than $3.4 million in fraud against TD Bank customers between 2021 and 2022; Lam pleaded guilty and faces up to 30 years.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; Charter confirmed a breach after being listed on the ShinyHunters dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: American telco confirmed the security breach; full scope of stolen data not yet disclosed.

incidents.victim: AI infrastructure operators (LiteLLM, vLLM, MCP servers using Starlette)
incidents.vector: A flaw in the Starlette Python web framework (CVE-2026-48710, 'BadHost') lets attackers craft a Host header that fools the server into treating private endpoints as public, bypassing authentication.
incidents.impact: Vulnerability disclosed and patched but a large share of AI server infrastructure remained unpatched; X41 D-Sec published exploit details and a scanner so defenders can check exposure.

incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a zero-day ViewState deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-5426) made possible because Digital Knowledge's KnowledgeDeliver LMS shipped with identical hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey values across customers.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained unauthenticated RCE on internet-facing LMS instances, deployed an in-memory web shell, modified site JavaScript to push a fake security plugin, and infected visitors with a Cobalt Strike payload keyed to the targeted organization's name.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries / MIRhosting / WorkTitans (and downstream Russia-linked operations)
incidents.attacker: Russia — state-linked espionage and hacktivist ecosystem (downstream users)
incidents.vector: Dutch FIOD seized more than 800 servers across two data centers and arrested two co-owners (Andrey Nesterenko and Youssef Zinad) for sanctions violations after EU-sanctioned Stark Industries' infrastructure was transferred to Dutch entity WorkTitans and connected to the internet via MIRhosting.
incidents.impact: MIRhosting and WorkTitans were the most-used networks in pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies during Denmark's municipal election week in November 2025; takedown disrupted infrastructure used for DDoS, influence operations, and sanctions evasion.

incidents.vector: Not publicly detailed.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people had medical data stolen — including biometric fingerprints and palm prints that cannot be replaced, raising long-tail identity-fraud exposure.

incidents.vector: Kali365 phishing platform abuses Microsoft OAuth device-code authorization flows: victims paste a code from an AI-generated lure into a legitimate Microsoft device page, granting attacker-controlled apps access to their M365 account and bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: FBI issued a public alert; the platform sells access for $250/month or $2,000/year and stores captured OAuth tokens that provide persistent access across Microsoft services without prompting for credentials or MFA again.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense, and technology firms in US, Israel, UAE, and Middle East
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with tailored recruitment lures (fake job application portals impersonating a global air carrier and a popular video-conferencing platform) deployed DLL-sideloaded RATs; the most recent campaigns used AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET app security.
incidents.impact: Six new remote-access trojan variants in two malware families deployed between February and April 2026, timed with the regional conflict that began February 28, 2026; targets spanned US, Israeli, UAE, and other Middle Eastern entities.

incidents.vector: Attackers used compromised credentials belonging to other Lithuanian government agencies that were authorized to query the registry.
incidents.impact: 600,000 records stolen, including property and cadastral details and real names of property owners.

incidents.vector: Elasticsearch database left exposed to the internet without authentication for at least two months.
incidents.impact: Personal details of nearly 19 million customers — including phone numbers and full names tied to WeChat accounts — were accessible before the server was secured.

incidents.victim: Australian MP Zali Steggall and three staffers
incidents.vector: WhatsApp account compromise consistent with an active Russian campaign targeting Signal/WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: Independent MP Steggall and three of her staff had their WhatsApp accounts breached in March 2026; suspected foreign state actor identified by Australian authorities.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; intrusions reportedly went undetected initially.
incidents.impact: Two government agencies storing data on millions of Vietnamese citizens were breached; investigation launched after detection.

incidents.victim: US Department of Defense IP ranges and other DDoS targets
incidents.vector: Operator built a fast-spreading IoT botnet that enslaved millions of digital photo frames, web cameras, and similar devices, then rented attack capacity and launched assaults including against DoD address space.
incidents.impact: Canadian authorities arrested 23-year-old Jacob Butler of Ottawa, charged in US and Canada; the botnet launched record-setting attacks measured near 30 Tbps and issued over 25,000 attack commands, with some victims reporting losses exceeding $1M.

incidents.victim: Cybercrime ecosystem users of First VPN
incidents.vector: First VPN, marketed on Russian-speaking cybercrime forums, hid attacker infrastructure and identities and was used in ransomware, fraud, and data-theft operations.
incidents.impact: Europol-led operation arrested the alleged administrator in Ukraine, dismantled 33 servers, seized multiple domains, and obtained the user database — feeding 21 follow-on investigations globally.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised the maintainer of the Nx Console VS Code extension, pushed a malicious extension version to the VS Code Marketplace, and used it to compromise a GitHub employee's device.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 GitHub-internal repositories were exfiltrated and offered for sale for $50,000 on a cybercrime forum; GitHub said no customer data was affected and rotated critical credentials the same day; Grafana also linked a separate breach to the same TanStack/Nx supply-chain incident.

incidents.victim: Cybercriminal ecosystem (Rhysida, INC, Qilin, Akira affiliates)
incidents.vector: Abused Microsoft Artifact Signing to mint fraudulent short-lived code-signing certificates so ransomware affiliates could disguise malware (Oyster, Lumma Stealer, Vidar) as legitimate software (AnyDesk, Teams, PuTTY, Webex) and bypass security controls.
incidents.impact: Microsoft seized Fox Tempest's website, took hundreds of VMs offline, and revoked over 1,000 certificates; the service had generated over 1,000 certificates and run hundreds of Azure tenants, and ransomware affiliates paid Fox Tempest millions of dollars.

incidents.vector: Specially crafted network traffic exploited a previously undisclosed flaw in Huawei enterprise router VRP software, sending devices into a continuous restart loop (no CVE issued ten months later).
incidents.impact: On July 23, 2025, landline, 4G, and 5G mobile networks went down across Luxembourg for more than three hours, leaving hundreds of thousands of residents unable to reach emergency services; the flaw remains publicly undisclosed and unpatched in any public advisory.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed by the attackers.
incidents.impact: Play ransomware group is extorting MyPillow and claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from its corporate network; the company has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Adversary injected malicious GitHub Actions workflows via more than 5,700 commits to compromised repositories, with payloads designed to harvest credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets from build pipelines.
incidents.impact: Over 5,500 GitHub repositories were infected in a single day, escalating downstream supply-chain risk for projects depending on the affected actions.

incidents.victim: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with administrative access disabled GitHub's secret-scanning protections and pushed AWS GovCloud keys, RSA private keys, and dozens of plaintext credentials for internal CISA systems to a public 'Private-CISA' GitHub profile.
incidents.impact: Repository was first created in November 2025 and exposed for months; an RSA private key gave attackers potential full access to every CISA-IT GitHub repository and CI/CD pipelines; more than a week after notification CISA was still rotating leaked credentials, and lawmakers in both chambers demanded answers.
